::: callout-note
## How to use this quiz

This quiz is designed as a **formative self-assessment tool**, not as a test.

Its purpose is to help you:
- check your understanding of the key concepts from Topic 8,
- identify which types of thinking you find more difficult, and
- guide your revision before the tutorial and future assessments.

### What this quiz measures

Each question belongs to one of four categories:

- **Subject Knowledge (SK):** definitions, concepts, and facts.  
- **Analysis (AN):** understanding relationships and economic mechanisms.  
- **Problem Solving (PS):** applying concepts to new situations.  
- **Mathematical Thinking (MT):** working with equations and quantitative relationships.

Your score will be broken down by category so you can see **where** you are strong and where you need more practice.

### How to complete the quiz

- You may use your notes and the lecture materials.
- Take your time — the goal is understanding, not speed.
- Use the **Hints** if you get stuck.
- You may refresh and retry the quiz as many times as you like.

### How to interpret your results

- A low score is **not a problem** — it tells you what to focus on.
- If you score low in:
  - **SK:** revise definitions and core concepts.
  - **AN:** revisit the logic of the models and examples.
  - **PS:** practise applying concepts to new cases.
  - **MT:** practise the mathematical calculations and equations.

### About the leaderboard

The leaderboard is optional and anonymous. It exists only to make practice more engaging.  
It has **no effect** on your grade and is not used for evaluation.

The only purpose of this quiz is to support your learning.

:::

```{r}
#| echo: false
library(webexercises)
```

<!-- FEEDBACK SCRIPT: interactive quiz with self-assessment -->
```{=html}
<script>
(function () {
  // 1) Configure your Google Apps Script Web App URL here.
  //    Example: https://script.google.com/macros/s/XXXXXXXXXXXX/exec
  const ENDPOINT = "https://script.google.com/macros/s/AKfycbysCOTW2ZLw5ruYY84Y-o0zB7nt0jkowiC3OoKJSdh2OYv-ZXa_1vTb_TU4BYwcwSZ0Jw/exec";

  const norm = s => (s || "").replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();

  function getSelectedLabelText(qEl) {
    const input = qEl.querySelector('input[type="radio"]:checked');
    if (!input) return "";
    const label = input.closest('label') || document.querySelector('label[for="' + input.id + '"]');
    return label ? norm(label.textContent) : "";
  }

  function clearFeedback(qEl) {
    qEl.querySelectorAll("label").forEach(l => l.classList.remove("is-correct", "is-incorrect"));
    const line = qEl.querySelector(".quiz-feedback-line");
    if (line) {
      line.textContent = "";
      line.classList.add("hidden");
    }
  }

  function setFeedback(qEl, isCorrect) {
    const line = qEl.querySelector(".quiz-feedback-line");
    if (!line) return;
    line.textContent = isCorrect ? "Correct." : "Incorrect.";
    line.classList.remove("hidden");
  }

  async function postAttempt(payload) {
    // Do not attempt POST if ENDPOINT is not configured
    if (!ENDPOINT || ENDPOINT.includes("PASTE_YOUR_")) return;

    try {
      await fetch(ENDPOINT, {
        method: "POST",
        mode: "no-cors",
        keepalive: true,
        body: JSON.stringify(payload)
      });
    } catch (err) {
      console.warn("Could not save attempt:", err);
    }
  }

  async function loadLeaderboard(quizName) {
    const table = document.getElementById("leaderboard");
    if (!table) return;

    // If not configured, show a friendly message and stop.
    if (!ENDPOINT || ENDPOINT.includes("PASTE_YOUR_")) {
      table.innerHTML = "<tr><td>Leaderboard is not configured yet. Add your Apps Script URL in the page source.</td></tr>";
      return;
    }

    try {
      const res = await fetch(ENDPOINT, { method: "GET" });
      if (!res.ok) throw new Error("HTTP " + res.status);
      const rows = await res.json();

      // Filter for this quiz only (defensive: older rows may not have the fields)
      const filtered = (rows || []).filter(r => String(r.quiz || "") === String(quizName));

      // Keep best score per nickname
      const best = new Map();
      filtered.forEach(r => {
        const nick = String(r.nickname || "").trim();
        if (!nick) return;
        const score = Number(r.score);
        const total = Number(r.total);
        const ts = new Date(r.timestamp || 0).getTime();

        const prev = best.get(nick);
        if (!prev || score > prev.score || (score === prev.score && ts < prev.ts)) {
          best.set(nick, { nickname: nick, score, total, ts });
        }
      });

      const leaderboard = Array.from(best.values())
        .sort((a, b) => (b.score - a.score) || (a.ts - b.ts))
        .slice(0, 30);

      if (leaderboard.length === 0) {
        table.innerHTML = "<tr><td>No attempts recorded yet.</td></tr>";
      } else {
        table.innerHTML =
          "<tr><th>Rank</th><th>Nickname</th><th>Score</th></tr>" +
          leaderboard.map((r, i) =>
            "<tr><td>" + (i + 1) + "</td><td>" + String(r.nickname) + "</td><td>" + r.score + " / " + r.total + "</td></tr>"
          ).join("");
      }

      // Load and display question statistics
      await loadQuestionStats(quizName, rows);
    } catch (err) {
      table.innerHTML = "<tr><td>Could not load leaderboard.</td></tr>";
      console.warn("Leaderboard error:", err);
    }
  }

  async function loadQuestionStats(quizName, allRows) {
    const statsContainer = document.getElementById("question-stats");
    if (!statsContainer) return;

    // Filter for this quiz only
    const filtered = (allRows || []).filter(r => String(r.quiz || "") === String(quizName));

    console.log("=== DEBUGGING QUESTION STATS ===");
    console.log("Filtered rows count:", filtered.length);
    if (filtered.length > 0) {
      console.log("Sample row:", filtered[0]);
    }

    // Build a map of question index to identifier
    const questionIdentifiers = {};
    document.querySelectorAll(".mcq-we-q").forEach((qEl, idx) => {
      const questionText = qEl.querySelector("strong")?.textContent || "";
      const categoryMatch = questionText.match(/^(SK|AN|PS|MT)(\d+)/);
      if (categoryMatch) {
        questionIdentifiers[idx] = categoryMatch[1] + categoryMatch[2];
      } else {
        questionIdentifiers[idx] = "Q" + (idx + 1);
      }
    });

    console.log("Question identifiers map:", questionIdentifiers);

    // Count incorrect attempts per question
    const questionStats = {};
    filtered.forEach((row, rowIdx) => {
      let details = row.details || {};
      
      // If details is a string (JSON), parse it
      if (typeof details === "string") {
        try {
          details = JSON.parse(details);
          console.log(`Row ${rowIdx} - Parsed details from string`);
        } catch (e) {
          console.warn(`Row ${rowIdx} - Could not parse details:`, details);
          return;
        }
      }

      console.log(`Row ${rowIdx} - Processing details:`, details);

      Object.entries(details).forEach(([questionId, qData]) => {
        if (!questionStats[questionId]) {
          questionStats[questionId] = { incorrectCount: 0, totalCount: 0 };
        }
        
        questionStats[questionId].totalCount += 1;
        
        // Check if answer was incorrect (ok: 0 means incorrect)
        const isIncorrect = qData.ok === 0;
        if (isIncorrect) {
          questionStats[questionId].incorrectCount += 1;
        }
      });
    });

    console.log("\nFinal question stats:", questionStats);

    // Get top 10 most incorrect questions, sorted by incorrect count
    const sortedQuestions = Object.entries(questionStats)
      .map(([qKey, stats]) => ({
        qKey: qKey,
        incorrectCount: stats.incorrectCount,
        totalCount: stats.totalCount,
        incorrectRate: stats.totalCount > 0 ? (stats.incorrectCount / stats.totalCount * 100).toFixed(1) : 0
      }))
      .sort((a, b) => b.incorrectCount - a.incorrectCount)
      .slice(0, 10);

    console.log("Sorted questions:", sortedQuestions);

    if (sortedQuestions.length === 0) {
      statsContainer.innerHTML = "<p>No question statistics available yet.</p>";
    } else {
      statsContainer.innerHTML =
        "<h4>Top 10 Questions with Most Incorrect Attempts</h4>" +
        "<table style='width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse;'>" +
        "<tr style='border-bottom: 2px solid #ccc;'><th style='text-align: left; padding: 8px;'>Question</th><th style='text-align: center; padding: 8px;'>Incorrect Attempts</th><th style='text-align: center; padding: 8px;'>Total Attempts</th><th style='text-align: center; padding: 8px;'>Incorrect Rate</th></tr>" +
        sortedQuestions.map(q =>
          "<tr style='border-bottom: 1px solid #eee;'>" +
          "<td style='padding: 8px;'>" + String(q.qKey) + "</td>" +
          "<td style='text-align: center; padding: 8px;'>" + q.incorrectCount + "</td>" +
          "<td style='text-align: center; padding: 8px;'>" + q.totalCount + "</td>" +
          "<td style='text-align: center; padding: 8px;'>" + q.incorrectRate + "%</td>" +
          "</tr>"
        ).join("") +
        "</table>";
    }
  }

  async function submitQuiz() {
    const nicknameEl = document.getElementById("nickname");
    const resultEl = document.getElementById("quiz-result");
    const submitBtn = document.getElementById("quiz-submit");

    const nickname = (nicknameEl?.value || "").trim();
    if (!nickname) {
      alert("Please enter a nickname before submitting.");
      nicknameEl?.focus();
      return;
    }

    // Lock submit to avoid double posting
    if (submitBtn) submitBtn.disabled = true;

    let score = 0;
    let total = 0;
    const details = {};
    
    // Category scores
    const categories = {
      SK: { score: 0, total: 0, name: "Subject Knowledge" },
      AN: { score: 0, total: 0, name: "Analysis" },
      PS: { score: 0, total: 0, name: "Problem Solving" },
      MT: { score: 0, total: 0, name: "Mathematical Thinking" }
    };

    const questions = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(".mcq-we-q"));

    // Clear any prior feedback first (important if student re-submits)
    questions.forEach(clearFeedback);

    questions.forEach((qEl, idx) => {
      total += 1;
      const keyEl = qEl.querySelector(".mcq-key");
      const correct = norm(keyEl?.getAttribute("data-correct") || "");
      const selected = getSelectedLabelText(qEl);

      const isCorrect = selected && (selected === correct);
      if (isCorrect) score += 1;

      // Extract category and question ID from question text (SK1, AN1, PS1, MT1, etc.)
      const questionText = qEl.querySelector("strong")?.textContent || "";
      const categoryMatch = questionText.match(/^(SK|AN|PS|MT)(\d+)/);
      let questionId = "Q" + (idx + 1);
      
      if (categoryMatch) {
        const cat = categoryMatch[1];
        const num = categoryMatch[2];
        questionId = cat + num;
        
        categories[cat].total += 1;
        if (isCorrect) categories[cat].score += 1;
      }

      details[questionId] = { selected, correct, ok: isCorrect ? 1 : 0 };

      // Mark only after submit
      if (selected) {
        const input = qEl.querySelector('input[type="radio"]:checked');
        const label = input?.closest("label") || (input ? document.querySelector('label[for="' + input.id + '"]') : null);
        if (label) label.classList.add(isCorrect ? "is-correct" : "is-incorrect");
      }
      setFeedback(qEl, isCorrect);
    });

    if (resultEl) {
      let resultHTML = "<strong>Overall Score: " + score + " / " + total + "</strong><br><br>";
      
      // Add category breakdown
      for (const key in categories) {
        const cat = categories[key];
        if (cat.total > 0) {
          resultHTML += cat.name + ": " + cat.score + " / " + cat.total + "<br>";
        }
      }
      
      // Add correct and incorrect questions
      const correctQuestions = [];
      const incorrectQuestions = [];
      
      questions.forEach((qEl, idx) => {
        const keyEl = qEl.querySelector(".mcq-key");
        const correct = norm(keyEl?.getAttribute("data-correct") || "");
        const selected = getSelectedLabelText(qEl);
        const isCorrect = selected && (selected === correct);
        
        // Extract question ID from question text
        const questionText = qEl.querySelector("strong")?.textContent || "";
        const categoryMatch = questionText.match(/^(SK|AN|PS|MT)(\d+)/);
        let questionId = "Q" + (idx + 1);
        if (categoryMatch) {
          questionId = categoryMatch[1] + categoryMatch[2];
        }
        
        if (selected) {
          if (isCorrect) {
            correctQuestions.push(questionId);
          } else {
            incorrectQuestions.push(questionId);
          }
        }
      });
      
      resultHTML += "<br><strong>Correct Questions:</strong> " + (correctQuestions.length > 0 ? correctQuestions.join(", ") : "None") + "<br>";
      resultHTML += "<strong>Incorrect Questions:</strong> " + (incorrectQuestions.length > 0 ? incorrectQuestions.join(", ") : "None") + "<br>";
      
      resultEl.innerHTML = resultHTML;
    }

    // Persist attempt (best practice: store what you need; nickname only = low GDPR footprint)
    await postAttempt({
      timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
      nickname,
      quiz: "Topic8",
      score,
      total,
      details
    });

    // Refresh leaderboard after a successful submit (or best-effort submit)
    await loadLeaderboard("Topic8");

    // Disable all radio buttons and submit button to prevent further changes
    document.querySelectorAll(".mcq-we-q input[type='radio']").forEach(input => {
      input.disabled = true;
    });
    if (submitBtn) submitBtn.disabled = true;
  }

  // Expose submitQuiz globally for the button onclick
  window.submitQuiz = submitQuiz;

  // Add a feedback line container to each question if it doesn't exist
  document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
    document.querySelectorAll(".mcq-we-q").forEach(qEl => {
      if (!qEl.querySelector(".quiz-feedback-line")) {
        const line = document.createElement("div");
        line.className = "quiz-feedback-line hidden";
        qEl.appendChild(line);
      }
    });

    loadLeaderboard("Topic8");
  });
})();
</script>
```

## Subject Knowledge

<div class="mcq-we-q">

`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Commercial banks", "Foreign governments", answer = "Short-term political pressure", "International organisations"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Short-term political pressure"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Think about time horizons in policymaking.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK2) Inflation targeting involves:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Fixing the exchange rate", answer = "Announcing a numerical inflation objective", "Targeting money growth exclusively", "Eliminating fiscal deficits"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Announcing a numerical inflation objective"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Transparency and numerical goals are key features.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">

`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Velocity is unstable", answer = "Policymakers may deviate from previously announced plans", "Exchange rates fluctuate", "Output is constant"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Policymakers may deviate from previously announced plans"></span>

</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK4) The inflation bias in discretionary policy occurs when:**

<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Policymakers attempt to exploit a short-run Phillips curve"></span>

</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">

`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Government spending", answer = "Expected inflation", "Velocity directly", "Reserve requirements"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Expected inflation"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Expectations of future policy shape current outcomes.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK6) A conservative central banker (Rogoff model) places:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Greater weight on output stabilisation", answer = "Greater weight on inflation stabilisation", "Equal weight on all objectives", "No weight on inflation"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Greater weight on inflation stabilisation"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Preference parameters differ from society's average.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK7) Rules-based policy differs from discretion because it:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Eliminates inflation", answer = "Commits policymakers to systematic responses", "Fixes exchange rates permanently", "Removes capital mobility"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Commits policymakers to systematic responses"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Commitment changes expectations formation.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK8) Forward guidance enhances credibility when it is:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Vague and flexible", answer = "Contingent and clearly communicated", "Secretive", "Unrelated to policy rules"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Contingent and clearly communicated"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Conditional commitments reduce uncertainty.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK9) An inflation-targeting regime with strong transparency primarily reduces:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Fiscal deficits", "Risk premia", answer = "Inflation volatility", "Velocity"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Inflation volatility"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Anchored expectations dampen fluctuations.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK10) The Barro-Gordon model predicts that under discretion, equilibrium inflation is:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Zero", "Lower than target", answer = "Higher than socially optimal", "Independent of expectations"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Higher than socially optimal"></span>

## Analysis

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN1) Why does discretionary policy generate inflation bias even when output returns to its natural level?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Because velocity rises", answer = "Because expectations adjust upward", "Because fiscal deficits increase", "Because exchange rates float"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Because expectations adjust upward"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Rational expectations eliminate systematic output gains.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN2) If a central bank gains credibility, expected inflation becomes:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("More volatile", "Less anchored", answer = "More stable", "Irrelevant"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="More stable"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Credible commitment shapes private-sector forecasts.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN3) Why can delegation to a conservative central banker reduce inflation without large output costs?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Because money supply shrinks", answer = "Because expectations adjust downward", "Because fiscal policy changes", "Because exchange rates fix automatically"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Because expectations adjust downward"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Lower expected inflation shifts the short-run Phillips curve.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN4) If policymakers attempt surprise inflation repeatedly, what happens over time?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Output permanently rises", answer = "Inflation expectations increase", "Inflation falls", "Velocity stabilises"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Inflation expectations increase"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Rational agents learn from repeated deviations.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN5) Why does commitment technology eliminate inflation bias?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("It removes expectations", answer = "It aligns incentives with announced targets", "It fixes exchange rates", "It raises unemployment permanently"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="It aligns incentives with announced targets"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Credible rules alter policymakers' incentives.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN6) If society places equal weight on inflation and output, but the central bank is more inflation-averse, what is the likely macro outcome?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Higher inflation variability", answer = "Lower average inflation", "Higher output volatility", "Fixed exchange rates"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Lower average inflation"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Preference parameters influence equilibrium inflation.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN7) Why can excessive conservatism increase output variability?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Because inflation disappears", answer = "Because the central bank reacts weakly to demand shocks", "Because fiscal policy expands", "Because capital flows stop"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Because the central bank reacts weakly to demand shocks"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Stabilisation trade-offs depend on policy weights.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN8) If a central bank announces a target but frequently misses it without explanation, credibility will:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Increase", "Remain unchanged", answer = "Decline", "Eliminate inflation"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Decline"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Reputation depends on consistent performance.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN9) Why does time inconsistency arise even when policymakers are benevolent?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Because they prefer inflation", answer = "Because short-run incentives differ from long-run plans", "Because velocity fluctuates", "Because exchange rates float"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Because short-run incentives differ from long-run plans"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Commitment problems stem from changing optimisation constraints.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN10) In the Barro-Gordon framework, why is surprise inflation ineffective systematically?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Because output is fixed", answer = "Because agents form rational expectations", "Because inflation is zero", "Because money supply is constant"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Because agents form rational expectations"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Anticipated policy has no real effects.</details>
</div>

## Problem Solving

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS1) A central bank promises low inflation but has a history of high inflation. What happens to expected inflation?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("It falls immediately", answer = "It remains high", "It becomes zero", "It becomes negative"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="It remains high"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Reputation influences expectation formation.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS2) Suppose inflation target is 2%, but policymakers attempt to push unemployment below its natural rate. What happens in the long run?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c(answer = "Inflation rises above 2%", "Inflation falls", "Unemployment permanently falls", "Output doubles"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Inflation rises above 2%"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Attempts to exploit Phillips curve create inflation bias.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS3) A newly independent central bank adopts inflation targeting and communicates clearly. What happens to inflation volatility over time?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("It increases", answer = "It decreases", "It is unchanged", "It disappears completely"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="It decreases"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Anchored expectations stabilise inflation dynamics.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS4) If policymakers can commit credibly, equilibrium inflation relative to discretion will be:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Higher", answer = "Lower", "The same", "Random"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Lower"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Commitment removes the incentive for surprise inflation.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS5) An economy experiences a negative supply shock. A highly conservative central bank reacts aggressively to inflation. What may happen to output?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Output stabilises fully", answer = "Output volatility increases", "Inflation doubles", "Exchange rate fixes"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Output volatility increases"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Strong anti-inflation response can amplify output losses.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS6) If expected inflation falls by 2pp due to increased credibility, what happens to nominal interest rates (holding real rate constant)?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Rise by 2pp", answer = "Fall by 2pp", "Stay unchanged", "Double"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Fall by 2pp"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Apply the Fisher equation.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS7) Under discretion, why might inflation remain positive even if target inflation is zero?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Because output gap is zero", answer = "Because inflation bias exists", "Because exchange rates float", "Because money supply contracts"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Because inflation bias exists"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Incentives to stimulate output create bias.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS8) If society delegates to a very conservative central banker, what trade-off arises?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Higher inflation and lower output", answer = "Lower inflation but potentially higher output volatility", "Fixed exchange rates", "Zero unemployment"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Lower inflation but potentially higher output volatility"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Preference weights affect stabilisation trade-offs.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS9) Why does reputational loss increase the cost of breaking a commitment?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Because inflation falls", answer = "Because future expectations become less anchored", "Because output rises", "Because money supply doubles"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Because future expectations become less anchored"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Reputation affects future policy effectiveness.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS10) If policymakers follow a strict rule that responds systematically to deviations, what happens to inflation expectations?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Become unanchored", answer = "Become more predictable", "Disappear", "Double"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Become more predictable"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Predictable policy improves expectation formation.</details>
</div>

## Mathematical Thinking

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT1) If the Phillips curve is $\pi = \pi^e - \alpha(u - u^*)$ and $u=u^*$, inflation equals:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("0", answer = "pi^e", "alpha", "-pi^e"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="pi^e"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Substitute carefully when the unemployment gap is zero.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT2) If expected inflation is 4% and real rate is 1%, nominal rate equals:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("3%", "4%", answer = "5%", "6%"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="5%"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Use $i = r + \pi^e$.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT3) If policymakers weight inflation twice as much as output, the loss function slope becomes:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Flatter", answer = "Steeper", "Zero", "Negative"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Steeper"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Higher inflation weight increases responsiveness.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT4) If inflation bias equals $\frac{\alpha}{\beta}k$, increasing $\beta$ (weight on inflation) makes bias:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Larger", answer = "Smaller", "Zero", "Infinite"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Smaller"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Examine the denominator.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT5) If unemployment gap is -2 and $\alpha=0.5$, inflation deviation equals:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("-1", "0", answer = "1", "2"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="1"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Multiply carefully and track signs.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT6) If credibility reduces expected inflation from 5% to 3%, and output gap is zero, inflation falls by:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("0%", answer = "2%", "3%", "5%"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="2%"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>With no gap, inflation equals expectations.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT7) If nominal rate is 6% and expected inflation drops from 4% to 2%, real rate rises by:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("0%", "1%", answer = "2%", "4%"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="2%"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Recalculate the real rate before and after.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT8) If $\alpha$ doubles, the Phillips curve becomes:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Flatter", answer = "Steeper", "Vertical", "Horizontal"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Steeper"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Sensitivity of inflation to unemployment gap increases.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT9) If inflation bias is 3% under discretion and zero under commitment, welfare improves because:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Output permanently rises", "Variance disappears", answer = "Average inflation falls without output loss", "Exchange rate fixes"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Average inflation falls without output loss"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Bias affects levels, not natural output.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT10) If policymakers attempt surprise inflation of 2% but expectations adjust fully, long-run output change equals:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("2%", "1%", answer = "0%", "-2%"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="0%"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Anticipated inflation has no real effect.</details>
</div>
